page: Microsoft Azure D16a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 410 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks position the D16a_v4 primarily in the average tier across most workloads. Single-core CPU performance is a notable strength, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics fall within the middle 50%. A key performance tradeoff is observed in memory write operations, where large-block write bandwidth is classified in the bottom 25%, contrasting with the average read-only memory bandwidth. Large-model LLM inference is not supported due to the lack of hardware accelerators, though small-model text generation performs strongly.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16a_v4 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, a moderate memory-to-vCPU ratio, and bundled local SSD storage makes it a viable option for applications requiring consistent CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. Recommended workloads include web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale text processing.

Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance and small-model text generation capabilities, while multi-core processing, database operations, and memory read bandwidth remain in the average tier. A notable hardware tradeoff is its weak large-block memory write bandwidth, which falls in the bottom 25%. Lacking dedicated GPUs, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for workloads requiring balanced compute and memory resources without specialized acceleration. It is well-suited for static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose database operations.
